A document with no setup refuses to post a rotary program on an A-only machine. The same program posts when the document has a setup.

## Steps

1. Take `examples/catalog/multiaxis/wrapped/build.camscript` from PR for #2869.
2. Remove the two lines `add_setup` and `set_setup_post`.
3. Run `cargo xtask catalog --case multiaxis/wrapped`.

Result: verification passes, and the post refuses with the warning above.

With the two lines, the program posts. It has A words only, and no B word.

The document post and a setup post on the same machine give the same program. A tool axis in the YZ plane needs only A on this machine. The post must not command B for it.

## Notes

- The refusal is safe: no wrong G-code goes out.
- The workaround is to add a setup and set its post.
- The program has Rotary Parallel passes that go all the way round the bar. The tool axis points straight down on the underside.
- Found during #2869. Part of #2392.

title: Fanuc post writes stream A/B words that a tilt-head chain (A carries B) reads as a different tool axis

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:multiaxis
labels.description: 3+2, 5-axis, rotary

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
## What happens

The Fanuc post writes the `A` and `B` words of the stream below `G43.4` without a change.
The stream letters follow the pose law `axis = Ry(B) · Rx(A) · Z` (`crates/cl/src/cl/pose.rs`, lines 10-14).
In that law, B is the outer rotation and A is the inner rotation.

The Tilt-head machine nests the rotaries in the opposite order.
In `assets/machines/tilthead.mch` (lines 11-14), the A rotary carries the B rotary, and B carries the head.
For the joint angles A and B, that chain gives the tool axis `Rx(A) · Ry(B) · Z`.

The two products are equal only when A or B is zero.
Thus the machine reads the posted words as a different tool axis.
No check refuses the program: `cam.verify()` is clean and the post completes.

## Evidence

The review of PR #4408 measured the program `examples/catalog/multiaxis/five-axis/five-axis.nc` at head e850da857 (https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/4408#issuecomment-7225976287):

- 2365 of 3357 feeds have A and B not zero.
- On 1882 feeds the two axes differ by more than 1 degree. On 1090 feeds they differ by more than 5 degrees.
- The largest difference is 27.3 degrees: `G01 X24.443 Y8.747 Z7.178 A-40.588 B68.859 F88.9`.
- With the pose law order, the deepest contact with the model is 0.054 mm. The tolerance of the operations is 0.1 mm.
- With the chain order of the machine file, the tool is up to 0.37 mm into the model, and 432 feeds are deeper than 0.15 mm.

Code on main (878f8c2f2):

- `assets/posts/fanuc.cps`, `tilt()`: writes `angleWord("A", p.A)` and `angleWord("B", p.B)` as they come. It refuses a missing letter and a reversed lone X rotary. It does not read the chain order.
- `crates/post/src/machine/trunnion.rs`, `rotary_axes()`: gives the rotaries in the chain order (`chain_order`). The tilt path of the post does not use it for the angles.
- `assets/machines/AGENTS.md`: "the nest chain is the kinematics".

## Assumption

This issue reads the nest of `tilthead.mch` as "A carries B".
If the maintainer decides that the nest means "B carries A", the posted words are correct.
Then the machine file or `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` must say so, and this issue closes with that change.

## Scope: the whole class

The defect is not special to one case or one machine.
Each machine that states two tilting rotaries can have a chain order that differs from the pose law order.
Each dialect that writes the stream letters as joint angles has the same defect on such a machine.

## Done means

- One rule holds for each machine with two tilting rotaries: the post (or the program gate) expresses the stream pose in the joint angles of the stated chain, or it refuses by name a chain that the dialect cannot express.
- A test pins the rule with a pose where A and B are not zero, on a chain where A carries B and on a chain where B carries A.
- The travel check judges the same joint angles that the post writes.
- No recorded program comes from the old behaviour.

## Found while

Found by the review of PR #4408 (catalog case `multiaxis/five-axis`, issue #2870).
The diff of that PR does not cause the defect. The case is held until this issue is decided.
Parent catalog issue: #2392.

## What happens

Some "holds" tests of the law suite (`crates/pathkernel/tests/laws/`) cannot fail:

- `l7_move.rs:32-35` and `:58-62`: the L7 holds test compares the kernel with its own output.
- `kit.rs:116-118` with `l5_entry.rs:24-28`, `l6_load.rs:18-21`, `l3_order.rs:32-39`: a refusal is recorded as held (0.0 against 0.0). A stage that always refuses passes each law.

## Problem

The README "Contributing" section does not tell a contributor how much work fits their AI subscription. A contributor with a small plan starts a large issue, runs out of quota, and the PR stalls half done. Some contributor agents also try to push to `NeoTech/Camcraft` or ask for maintainer-only API reads, instead of the fork flow.

## Change

Add a subsection `### How you can help, by AI budget` to the README "Contributing" section (after "Tools"). Write it in ASD-STE100. Content:

1. A table: budget tier -> what to pick -> what to avoid.
   - No AI subscription: test on a real machine (air or foam cuts), report bugs with the posted program, send the control's programming manual, check docs.
   - Small plan (about USD 20 a month; a few hours of this project per week): `effort:low` issues (docs, labels, a test fixture, a string); one small PR at a time; reviews of a single small PR.
   - Medium plan: `effort:medium` issues (one crate, a known pattern).

2. "If you run out of quota": open the PR as a draft with what you have, tick "Allow edits by maintainers", and comment `help me finish`. Maintainers build, test and finish it.
3. "You do not need a big disk": the review boxes build and test each PR. Run only the tests of your change, or none.
4. Fork flow reminder, in four lines: work on a branch in your fork; open the PR from that branch into `NeoTech/Camcraft:main`; push review fixes to the same branch; merge `main` into it, never rebase or force-push an open PR. Do not push to `NeoTech/Camcraft`. Ask ownership questions on the PR; a maintainer answers.

Docs only. No code change.

title: Contributor ownership verification requires collaborators API access unavailable to fork contributors

body:
## Problem

The branch-writer/reviewer ownership procedure requires a collaborators API read that an outside contributor cannot perform. This leaves no documented path for a contributor to resume requested follow-up work after a reviewer releases ownership.

Account: `seelesturm`, contributing from `seelesturm/Camcraft-NeoTech` to `NeoTech/Camcraft`.

## Required procedure

In [ownership.md](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/main/.claude/skills/issue-claims/references/ownership.md), the **Record and read** section requires verifying both the reviewer record author and the reviewer login against base-repository collaborators with `permissions.push`, using the paginated collaborators API. It says failed authority reads mean STOP.

The **Before dispatch** section then requires applying those author checks before treating a record as an owner. This affects contributor writer handoff after review, not only someone attempting a counted collaborator review.

## Reproduction

Authenticate as an outside contributor without upstream push access, then run:

```sh
gh api --paginate repos/NeoTech/Camcraft/collaborators
```

Actual response, reproduced on November 27, 2026:

```json
{
  "message": "Must have push access to view repository collaborators.",
  "documentation_url": "https://docs.github.com/rest/collaborators/collaborators#list-repository-collaborators",
  "status": "403"
}
```

## Concrete effect

On #4378, the collaborator's code review and local checks passed. The remaining request is to publish existing before/after viewport images on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch and link them from the PR body. The reviewer explicitly released ownership:

- [Review and requested evidence](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/4378#issuecomment-7222407129)
- [Reviewer release](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/4378#issuecomment-7222411863)

The contributor can read those public records, but the prescribed authority verification fails before recording the next evidence writer. No failed screenshot push or PR-body update is being reported: the stop occurs at the procedural prerequisite.

The same procedure question was already raised for #4238:
[existing contributor clarification request](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/4238#issuecomment-7206685402).
It also affects the corrective follow-up described on merged #4319:
[correction notice and writer-procedure question](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/4319#issuecomment-7212134672).

## Expected behavior / requested resolution

@mkinney: please document a contributor-compatible way to verify the relevant reviewer authority and resume writer work, or explicitly clarify when a public reviewer result/release allows that handoff without the collaborators API read.

The procedure should preserve the distinction between contributor pre-checks and counted collaborator reviews, and retain the checks for active owners and unexpected remote-head changes.

No upstream write access, counted-review authority or merge permission is requested. The desired fix is a documented contribution procedure that outside contributors can actually follow.

## What happens

The generic wire ISO post writes every EDM code from the machine file's `edm.codes`. A machine file cannot make it write a program that a Charmilles CT-Millennium or GF AgieCharmilles ISO control accepts and fully sets up. No shipped machine file targets these controls, so this is support for a new dialect. These items are missing:

- the origin word, or no work-offset word,
- the plane-height template,
- the corner codes,
- the tank and flushing codes,
- the table-load lines,
- the meaning of the U V words.

title: Wire ISO post: I and J are rounded apart from the written start, so the two arc radii can differ by more than 0.002 mm

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What happens

The wire ISO post writes `I` and `J` as `fu(c.I - p.StartX)` and `fu(c.J - p.StartY)`. It rounds the increment from the unrounded start point. The control adds the increment to the written (rounded) start. Thus the centre that the control reads moves by up to one output step on each axis, and the end point is also rounded.

In inch the post writes 4 decimals (0.00254 mm per step). The start radius and the end radius that the control calculates can then differ by about 0.005 mm. In mm the difference can reach about 0.002 mm. The GF AgieCharmilles ISO programming manual gives an arc check of 0.002 mm, and the control stops with an alarm above it.

## Expected

- `I` and `J` are calculated from the written start and the written centre.
- Inch output uses 5 decimals, as the control's inch input permits.
- The radius difference of the written words stays at or below 0.002 mm, or the post refuses the arc by name.

## Evidence (upstream main `eafe6aec6`)

- `assets/posts/wire-iso.cps:105`: `fu()` writes 4 decimals in inch.
- `assets/posts/wire-iso.cps:439-447`: the arc block.
- Not the same defect as #3474 (an arc that reads as a full turn).

Workaround: post the program in mm.

Found by the post audit against the GF AgieCharmilles manuals (#4130).

## Done means

A test posts small inch and mm arcs. It calculates the two radii from the written words and checks that they differ by no more than 0.002 mm.

body:
## Summary

This issue is a proposal from the two UI owners. It shows the target workspace in two mockups. It also gives the plan: the issues and pull requests that we intend to make, and the release order.

We ask the maintainer to read it and to answer the questions at the end. We do not file the sub-issues before the maintainer answers.

## Goal and limits

- CamCraft must feel like a CAM tool. A person who knows a CAM system must find the setup tree, the operation properties, Generate, Simulate and Post without a manual.
- The workspace must work on a small screen. Each side pane folds, so the viewport gets more space.
- No change in this plan changes a toolpath or posted G-code. The UI pull requests change only the look, the layout and the messages.
- Each change from the UI stays an undoable command. The MCP tools stay the same.
- Clean room: the mockups are our own drawings. We used no text, icons, layout or screenshots from another CAM product.

## Mockups

Both mockups are 1366 × 768. The source file is a FigCraft file in our design notes. They use the design language of research note 3: flat docked panes, neutral grey with a blue accent, IBM Plex Sans and IBM Plex Mono (SIL OFL), and the CamCraft icons from `assets/ui/`.

### E1: all panes open

![E1: all panes open](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/ui-proposal-images/ui-proposal/E1-proposal.png)

- Title bar: menu bar, Save, Undo and Redo, and document tabs. The second tab shows the target. Until CamCraft can open more than one file, there is one tab. The magnifier is a placeholder for a command search.
- Ribbon: a machine-mode list ("Milling") and workflow tabs in program order: Setup, 2D, 3D, Drill, Multi-axis, Simulate, Post. The ribbon shows only the groups of the selected tab.
- Browser: the setup first (stock, machine, then the operations in program order). Each operation shows its state as a symbol and a word: current, never, calculating (elapsed time), stale, failed. "Machine: not set · Choose…" is a warning that you can click.
- Viewport: the height planes have a key with the name of the operation, and labels in the scene.
- Properties: the operation editor has six groups: Tool and cutting data, Geometry, Heights, Passes, Entry and linking, Accuracy and output. A folded group shows its values on one line. Each height shows its reference, its offset and the result: "= Z 10.000 in G54". A small text tag shows the source of each value: default, template, derived or set. A disabled button tells why it is disabled. Delete is in the ⋯ menu.
- Issues pane, below the viewport: each issue names its cause and has one button that goes to the fix. A check that did not run shows as "unavailable", never as "passed". The running job shows its elapsed time and Cancel.

### E2: all panes folded

![E2: all panes folded](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/ui-proposal-images/ui-proposal/E2-proposal-folded.png)

- A folded side pane becomes a title chip on the viewport. The viewport then uses the full width. A click on a chip opens the pane again. The camera does not move when a pane folds or opens.
- Each chip keeps the safety state as text. The Browser chip shows the counts of failed and stale operations. The Properties chip shows the state of the operation.
- The issues pane folds to one line. The line keeps the counts and the running job with Cancel.
- The move-type key lists only the move types that the project contains. A hover tag on a move shows the operation, the move type and the feed rate.

Parts of E1 and E2 need engine work first: the source badges, the "failed" state, and a stop inside the generators. The section "Plan, step 2" names them.

## What CamCraft has today

We checked the code on `main`:

- Heights already have a reference and an offset (`HeightReference` in `crates/app/src/operation/types/height.rs`). The UI can show the result now.
- An operation has three states: Never, Ok and Stale (`OpStatus` in `crates/app/src/operation/types/sel.rs`).
- The windowed app generates toolpaths on a worker thread, with a progress overlay and Cancel (#2257). Cancel discards the result, but the worker continues to the end.
- The toolpath data has three move kinds: Rapid, Feed and Plunge (`crates/cl/src/cl/moves.rs`).
- CamCraft opens one project at a time.

## Plan, step 0: the UI kit crate

The maintainer asked on Discord to collect the UI/UX work into a crate. We propose a new crate `crates/ui-kit` (`camcraft-ui-kit`) for the design system.

- The crate depends on `egui` only. It does not depend on `camcraft-app`.
- It holds the tokens and the theme: colour roles, sizes, the theme-file reader and the contrast checks.
- It holds the components:
  - the pane frame, which folds to a title chip;
  - the title chips;
  - the ribbon cell and its groups;
  - the form row with units, the source badge and the result line;
  - the folded group with its summary line;
  - the status card for never, current, stale, calculating and failed;
  - the action band with the reasons for disabled buttons;
  - the keys for the heights and the move types;
  - the issue row.
- Each component takes plain data and returns the choice of the user. A component does not read the document. `crates/ui` keeps the panes. It changes the document into plain data, and it changes the choice into an undoable command.
- A small gallery binary shows each component in each state, in the light and the dark theme. Reviewers use it to compare the code with the mockups.

Why a crate:

1. The dependency graph makes the design rules true: a component cannot read the document, because the crate cannot see `camcraft-app`.
2. The crate compiles without flecs and the engine. Its tests (layout, contrast, AccessKit labels) run fast.
3. The look is in one place. A later palette (for example #655) maps onto one crate.

| PR | Content | Effort | Needs |
|---|---|---|---|
| K | Make the crate, with the decision entry for the new crate edge `ui → ui-kit` (AGENTS.md "No new dependency between our crates without a decision"). Move the theme tokens into it. Add the gallery binary. | high | R |

The later PRs build their components in the kit, and `crates/ui` keeps only the link to the app:

- B: form row, group, status card, action band.
- P: pane frame and title chips.
- D: ribbon cell.
- C1 and C2: the keys.
- I: the issue row.

We move existing code (the theme, the form seam) in the PR that touches it, never in one large move.

## Plan, step 1: UI work on what exists

These pull requests change no engine data. Each one is a `feat` PR in the enhancement lane, `P6`. Each one keeps toolpaths and posts the same, updates its `layout_page_*` and structural tests, and keeps the `crates/ui` test count (#1953).

| PR | Content | Effort | Needs |

title: Picks: a face pick on a .sc model follows its face by the SolidCraft name when the model imports again

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P8
labels.description: Larger idea needing design or research before code

body:
Part of #3915. Uses #4212.

**What happens now**
- A face pick is a hash of the face geometry (`crates/geometry/src/geometry/feature.rs:884`). When a design change moves the face or changes its size, the id is gone, and generate refuses the pick: "Face of 'part' is no longer in the model: re-pick it".
- Baseline on 0.27.0 (https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/3915#issuecomment-7201006498): the bracket at 60 mm, then 80 mm. The features of 8 of the 11 SolidCraft faces were lost, and generate refused the operations on them. The 80 mm file holds the same 11 names.
- CamCraft does not guess that a missing face and an added face are the same face: "re-picking is Stage C's decision, made visible to the user, never assumed" (`crates/geometry/src/geometry/revision.rs:17-20`). A SolidCraft name is not a guess. It is SolidCraft's own identity for the face. But the follow must be visible (Q2).

**Need**
- When a `.sc` model imports again, a face pick on it follows its face by its SolidCraft name.
- A pick that cannot follow is named in the re-import report, and generate refuses it as today.
- The geometry still decides. A pick follows only when exactly one new face has the same name set and the same kind (plane, or not a plane).
  - A CamCraft face or patch over several SolidCraft faces has a set of names.
  - A new face whose `former` is equal to an old name counts as a face with that name.
  - A name that is not `verified`: no follow.
- A pick whose id is still in the model does not change.
- Scope: the picks that operations hold (the geometry selection, area picks, "Do not touch" picks, and the pick stores of each kind). Setup, WCS, alignment, fixture and electrode picks behave as today. Start and exit picks are coordinates, not feature ids, so they behave as today.
- The follow also works when the project was saved and opened again, or runs headless, before the new revision arrives.
- The re-import and the follows are one undo step.
- A model with no names behaves as today.

**Questions for the maintainer**
- **Q1. A `PROJECT_VERSION` step?** The follow in a reopened project needs data from the earlier import, so the solution can save data in the project file. If it does, does that data need a version step?
  - `solids` (#917) has no step: "an old reader that drops it reads the soup" (`crates/app/src/project/entity.rs:637-644`).
  - `source` (#2463) came with v72: "An old reader must refuse a v72 file" (`crates/app/src/project/source_dto.rs:1-5`).
  - Recommended: no step. An old reader that drops the data gives today's behaviour, as with `solids`. A step also lands only at a cut, and older builds then refuse each file that the new build saves.
- **Q2. Follow automatically, or offer the follow?**
  - Follow at re-import, and add a needs-review line to each operation that has a followed pick; or
  - offer the follows as one step that the user or the agent accepts.
  - Recommended: follow, with a needs-review line that names the face, for example "face 'F2:side:b' of 'part' followed by its SolidCraft name after the model was imported again". It is one undo step, it is visible, and `mark_operation_reviewed` clears it (`crates/app/src/mcp/order_tools.rs:24`). Today the `needs_review` field of an operation (`crates/app/src/project/entity.rs:442`) holds migration warnings; this is a second use.
- **Q3. Do `Patch` picks follow in this sub-issue?**
  - Recommended: yes, by name set.
  - 2D Pocket takes a patch pick. In the baseline, the bracket's patch over three SolidCraft faces has the same name set in both files.

**Done means**
- Two revisions of one design, with the same names in a different order (fixtures as Q4 in #4212 decides):
  - a face pick on a face that moved or changed size follows by its name;
  - a `Patch` pick follows by its name set (if Q3 is yes);
  - a pick on a removed face does not follow: the re-import report names it, and generate refuses it as today;
  - an unverified name, two candidates, or a change of kind: no follow;
  - a `former` name follows;
  - each operation with a followed pick shows the follow (as Q2 decides);
  - undo puts back the old picks, and redo makes the follow again;
  - import, save, open, then import again: the follow works.
- STL, OBJ, STEP and a `.sc` with no names: the same behaviour as today.

I prepared this issue with Claude Code (an AI agent) and checked it.

title: Import: keep the SolidCraft source face and its name for each facet of a .sc model

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P8
labels.description: Larger idea needing design or research before code

body:
Part of #3915.

**What happens now**
- A `.sc` model comes from one SolidCraft body. The kernel knows the record face of each triangle (`MachiningMesh::tri_face`, `crates/kernel/src/machining_mesh.rs:46`).
- The import drops it. `push_facets` copies only the three corners (`crates/geometry/src/kernel_import.rs:13-26`).
- The `.sc` reader does not read the face names.
- SolidCraft writes one name for each face of the body record, in record order, in `cache/model.json` at `model.names[n].faces`. Each face also has `info`: `[aliases, bounds, verified, synonyms]`, and from SolidCraft 0.50.0 an optional fifth item, `former`. The research comments in #3915 give the sources and the runs.

**Need**
- After a `.sc` import, CamCraft knows for each facet its source face and the SolidCraft name of that face, with its `verified` flag and its `former` name.
- The import never fails because of names. Name data with a wrong count, a wrong shape or a value out of bounds gives no names, and the import continues as today.
- When the facets change by a different route (for example `repair_model`), the names must not stay on the wrong facets.
- STL, OBJ, STEP and a `.sc` file with no names: no names.
- A user sees no change in behaviour from this sub-issue. The other sub-issues of #3915 (picks, MCP) use the names.

**Questions for the maintainer**
- **Q5. Names from cache format 10 only?**
  - Format 10 is the format of SolidCraft's published names writer (`crates/doc/src/model_cache.rs`).
  - CamCraft knows format 8 only from the sample `testdata/models/solidcraft_for_beginners.sc` (`crates/kernel/src/solidcraft/mod.rs:51-53`), and the reader takes no layout from sample bytes (`mod.rs:15`).
  - Recommended: format 10 only. A format-8 model imports as today, with no names.
- **Q4. Which fixtures?** The options:
  - containers that the tests build in code, with names of our own, as `crates/kernel/tests/solidcraft_import/` already does;
  - `testdata/models/hole_on_pocket_wall.sc` (cache format 10, with names);
  - a pair that SolidCraft made from its `examples/bracket.json`, at `width` 60 mm and 80 mm.
  - Recommended: the containers that the tests build, first. Also `hole_on_pocket_wall.sc` if your rule on SolidCraft material permits it. The SolidCraft-made pair only with your permission.
  - The same choice applies to the tests of the other sub-issues.

**Done means**
- After a `.sc` import (cache format 10), each facet has its source face, and the SolidCraft name, `verified` flag and `former` name of that face. `info` with four items and with five items both read.
- A test shows that each facet gets the name of the face that it lies on, not only the correct count of names. (Facets that shift by one also give the correct count.)
- Bad name data gives no names, and the import is OK. The hostile-input tests cover the names part with no panic.
- STL, OBJ, STEP, a format-8 `.sc` and a `.sc` with no names: no names, and the behaviour is the same as today.

I prepared this issue with Claude Code (an AI agent) and checked it.

title: STEP import: a 3.7 MB twisted rotor passes the 300s kernel import bound and cancels

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
﻿## What happens

Importing a 3.7 MB STEP file of a twisted rotor passes the kernel import's 300 s bound and cancels. The import log line:

```
WARN camcraft_geometry::kernel_import: STEP import passed its 300s bound; cancelling
```

File: Rotor.STEP, 3,723,412 bytes, twisted rotor with curved faces. Retry gives the same result (deterministic).

## Why it matters

A user with a legitimate twisted-geometry part cannot import it at all through the STEP path - the only path for B-rep. The import does not resume or part-complete; the whole operation cancels.

## Reproduction

Import Rotor.STEP (available from the reporter) on Windows x64. The import runs the full 300 s, then the cooperative cancellation fires.

## Possible directions

- Raise or make the bound configurable is not the fix - the import is kernel-bound, single-threaded B-rep sewing. 300 s was already a generous budget.
- Profile where the kernel time goes (sewing? facetting? the fit stage of #2718/#2754?) and see whether the curved-face boundary splitting dominates.
- An interim escape: the user exports a mesh from the CAD side and imports STL/OBJ, which is fast - but loses B-rep fidelity for the fidelity checks.

Suggested labels: P3, area:geometry, effort:high, source:agent.

body:
The v0.27.0 cut gate (cut.yml, stage gate, 2026-11-26 00:17Z) stopped at step [01] "debug build (--no-run)" after 22.2 min. No test ran and none failed (summary: "0 failed, 1 stalled").

What happened: the step compiled until about 00:25Z. Then three `rust-lld` links ran at the same time (the `camcraft-ui` test binaries, cold build, `-j 4`, `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`). The links wrote no output for 15 min. The stall watchdog (`xtask/src/watchdog.rs`, default 15 min for a debug step, `CAMCRAFT_GATE_STALL_MIN` not set) then killed the process tree. The tag stage was skipped.

Why it is a bug: a `--no-run` build step is a build, not a test. A cold link of a large test binary can be silent for longer than a test step. The watchdog cannot tell a slow link from a hang, so a cut on a cold runner can fail with no code fault.

Possible fixes (choose one):
1. Give build steps (`--no-run`) the longer limit that `--release` and `--ignored` steps already get (4x).
2. Count child-process CPU time (rustc, rust-lld, cc) as progress, and stall only when the tree is idle.
3. Set `CAMCRAFT_GATE_STALL_MIN` for the gate step in `cut.yml` (a workaround, not a fix).

Workaround for the current cut: re-run the gate with `CAMCRAFT_GATE_STALL_MIN=45` in the cut runner's environment.

Related: #3493 (how the watchdog kills a step; this issue is about when).

Done means: a cold release-tier gate on the cut runner passes step [01] without a stall, and a unit test in `xtask` pins the build-step limit.

body:
## Goal

HEIDENHAIN controls accept different program words per control and per NC software version. Today:
- the Klartext post accepts only iTNC 530 NC 340490-03;
- the DIN/ISO post writes words that are valid only on newer software (#4093, #4094).

The posts should read the control facts that the machine file already states and write the matching dialect. A control or version that a post cannot serve is refused by name.

## The machine file (no new field)

`controller.identity` already holds the facts (#3181, `assets/machines/AGENTS.md`):

```json
"controller": {
  "post": "Heidenhain Klartext",
  "identity": { "model": "iTNC 530", "nc_software": "340490-03", "installed_options": ["1", "19"] }
}
```

Proposal: keep the file to facts only. Make the values canonical:
- `model`: as HEIDENHAIN writes it (`TNC 320`, `iTNC 530`, `TNC 640`, `TNC7`, ...).
- `nc_software`: 6-digit ID, `-`, 2-digit release, optional ` SP<n>`.
- `installed_options`: HEIDENHAIN option numbers as strings.

A missing `installed_options` means "unknown": the post refuses or warns for functions that need an option.

## Capability flags (derived from model + NC software + options)

One shared resolver gives each post a flag set. The main flags, each with its HEIDENHAIN version source in the research notes:

- `language.iso`: DIN/ISO exists (none on TNC 124/128/310; TNC 320 from 340 55x-04; TNC 620 from 340 56x-02; TNC 426/430 from 280 472; TNC7 from 81762x-17).
- `blockForm`: `contour`, or `paraxial` for TNC 124/128 (one axis per block, no arcs): refuse.
- `decimals`: 3 (TNC 124/310/410) or 4.
- `toolCallByName`, `toolNameMax` (16, or 32 from TNC 640 34059x-02), `toolDefLR` (false on TNC7 from 81762x-19).
- `drill.c200` / `drill.c205`: the cycle parameter level. Q379/Q253 from iTNC 340 422. Q208/Q395 only from iTNC 60642x-04, TNC 640 34059x-04, TNC 620 81760x-01, TNC 320 77185x-05.
- `oldCycles`: cycles 1/2/17 definable, run-only (iTNC from 340 422) or absent.
- `preset.cycle247`: cycle 247 sets a datum value before iTNC 340 422, and activates a preset-table row after it.
- `dwell`: cycle 9 / `G04 F`, or `FUNCTION DWELL` (TNC 640 -07, TNC 620 -04, TNC 320 -04, TNC7; never on iTNC 530).
- `tilt` (none / cycle 19 / PLANE), `planeAxial`, `planeSym`; `tcpm.kt` / `tcpm.iso` (M128 or FUNCTION TCPM; ISO FUNCTION TCPM only from TNC 640 34059x-10 / TNC 620 81760x-07).
- `m140`, `m136m137`, `feedFzFu`, `arcs.spatial`, `arcs.helixLin`, `q.qs`, `q.qlqr`, `q.formulaPriority2020` (TNC 640 34059x-11: always write parentheses).
- Option gating: tilting needs option 8 (iTNC: 1), TCPM option 9 (iTNC: 2), and on TNC 620 cycles 201-205/208/209 need option 19.

The profile table (control and version range to flag values) is in the research notes. It covers TNC 310, 410, 426/430, iTNC 530 (four profiles), TNC 320, TNC 620, TNC 640 and TNC7.

## What the posts branch on

- **Klartext:** profile check (replaces the fixed 340490-03 check), tool call form, the `M140` retract or `L Z.. M91/M92`, cycle 247, dwell form, and later the drilling cycles and the cycle parameter level.
- **DIN/ISO:** refuse when `language.iso` is false; the G200/G205 parameter level; always `G04 F` for a dwell unless `FUNCTION DWELL` is confirmed for ISO programs; `G247` only with the preset-table meaning; the coordinate format.

## Scope and order

1. The resolver and flags in one place (post engine or a shared post helper), with a table test: control + version → flags.
2. The DIN/ISO post uses it for the fixes in #4093 and #4094 (these can land first with a narrow check, and move to the resolver here).
3. The Klartext post uses it, and serves more than 340490-03.
4. A refusal by name for an unknown model or version (no silent fallback, because cycle 247 changes meaning between versions).

## Done means

- The resolver maps each control/version in the profile table to its flags. A table test pins it.
- Both posts branch on the flags, not on fixed version strings.
- An unknown control or version is refused by name.
- The goldens of the shipped Picomax machine file do not change, except for the fixes of #4093 and #4094.

Source: HEIDENHAIN's public manuals and "Overview of New and Modified Software Functions" documents, collected and compared by the author's agent (notes, not in the repository). Related: #3095, #3181, #4085, #4086, #4087, #4088, #4093, #4094.

body:
## The maintainer's words

2026-11-25: "Well we need a unifying approach to this planning and it calls for a motion planning kernel that dictates how motion can be implemented"

## Problem

Strategies have their own pass planners, link code and entry code. The same selection can give rings in one strategy and straight slots in another. A fix in one planner does not reach the others. #3743 designed a shared ring planner for 2D. This issue makes that design one kernel with a contract.

## The pipeline

1. Region: selection (edge, face, chain, points joined by lines), material side, bounds.
2. Guide curves: rings (concentric or morphed), rows, medial lines.
3. Load control: none, trochoidal, constant engagement. It changes a guide curve.
4. Order: start side (inside or outside) and direction.
5. Link: stay at depth. Lift only with a named reason.
6. Entry and exit: air entry, pre-drilled hole, cleared column, helix, ramp, arc, plunge.

A strategy is a set of choices for these stages. A strategy has no planner of its own.

## Laws

- The same region and the same guide choice give the same curves.
- The material side and the start side are separate parameters.
- The start side changes only the order and the start point.
- A fallback is visible. The status line names it.
- An entry into material needs a proof. Else the kernel refuses with a reason.
- A cut above the engagement limit is prevented or named.
- A move that migrates keeps its output. A defect fix is a separate change.

## Names

Use "path kernel" (for example `crates/motion/src/path_kernel/`). "Kernel" already means the geometry kernel and a heavy lane.

## Order of the steps

1. K0, the design record. #3750 can start at the same time, because it keeps its output.
2. K1.
3. K4 (order and link) and K5 (entry and exit).
4. K3 (load control) and K6 (move the strategies).
5. K7 grows with each step.

## Sub-issues

| Step | Content | Issues |
|---|---|---|
| K0 | Design record: stage types, laws, scope | #4024 |
| K1 | Region model: selection, material side, bounds | #4025 |
| K2 | Guide curves | #3750, #3788 |
| K3 | Load control | #4026, #3932, #3933, #3849 |
| K4 | Order and link | #3750, #3757, #3758 |
| K5 | Entry and exit | #3746, #3934, #3759, #3397 |
| K6 | Move the strategies | #3752, #3753, #3754, #3755, #3756, #3760 |
| K7 | One test suite for the laws | #4027 |

## Related issues

- Start and exit picks (#3325, #3327, #3329) stay separate. They use the start point of K4.
- #3323 is `P?`. It is only linked here.
- #3743 and #3741 are the earlier research and report.

## Scope

2D milling comes first. Then the 3D Pocket levels. 3D finishing, multi-axis, turning, sheet and EDM are not in this issue.

## Done means

Each 2D milling strategy plans through the kernel. The K7 suite is green. No strategy has its own ring, link or entry code.

body:
**Problem.** The built-in holder library (`crates/tools/src/holder_library*.rs`) has these holders:

- BT30, BT40 and CAT40, each with an ER collet chuck and a Weldon side-lock version;
- standalone ER11-ER40 collet chucks;
- Tormach TTS (ER20 and Weldon).

Many common spindle tapers and clamping types are missing. A user with such a machine must draw the holder (tool editor, #93) or import a DXF outline. Collision checks and simulation then depend on a hand-made shape.

**Missing, most common first:**

1. **HSK**: A63, E40, E32 and F63. These are common on routers and newer mills.
2. **SK / ISO / DIN 69871** (SK30, SK40) and **ISO 20/25/30** (automatic tool change router spindles).
3. **R8**: manual and small CNC knee mills.
4. **Shrink-fit holders** on the tapers above.

Then: CAT30, CAT50 and BT50; Morse taper; NMTB; hydraulic and milling (end-mill) chucks; ER50 and TG collets.

**Rules for each holder** (the same as `holder_library.rs`):

- Take the dimensions from the published standard dimension tables. Record each number and its source in a `docs/decisions/` file.
- Draw a conservative, typical outline: never smaller than the steel. Do not copy a vendor model.
- Add tests in the same form as `holder_library_tests.rs`.

This is under the safety floor, because the holder outline goes into the collision and gouge checks (`effort:high`).

**Coordination.** Do this together with qsmits's Tool library work: #3897 (U6, Holders list and holder view) and #3895 (U4, holder, stick-out and gauge length). Also see #3648 (component library and compatible-holder filter). Add a new holder type in the shape that U6 uses, so that the holder list shows it.

**Done means:** each holder in groups 1-4 is in the built-in library, with its standard source in a decision file and a pinning test. It can be selected for a tool in the tool library window. Users can add more holder types, as follow-ups, in this issue's comments.

body:
## Summary

This issue proposes a new design for the tool library. It is a proposal for discussion. It contains no code.

The "Tool library" tab on the right side becomes one dialog. The **Tools** cell of the ribbon opens it. The dialog has two kinds of item: tools and holders. Each kind has a list, a rail and an editor with a large drawing.

### Pictures

**1. Tool list** (Document, My library, Catalog; categories on the left)
![Tool list](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/1acd3beb0b0e9378b06074e3e2615ba7cd5d89f4/tool-library-proposal/1-tool-list.png)

**2. Tool editor** (the list is a rail; parameters, the assembly group and the drawing)
![Tool editor](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/1acd3beb0b0e9378b06074e3e2615ba7cd5d89f4/tool-library-proposal/2-tool-editor.png)

**3. Recipes tab**
![Recipes tab](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/1acd3beb0b0e9378b06074e3e2615ba7cd5d89f4/tool-library-proposal/3-recipes.png)

**4. Holder list**
![Holder list](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/1acd3beb0b0e9378b06074e3e2615ba7cd5d89f4/tool-library-proposal/4-holder-list.png)

**5. Holder editor**
![Holder editor](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/1acd3beb0b0e9378b06074e3e2615ba7cd5d89f4/tool-library-proposal/5-holder-editor.png)

Interactive mock-up (one HTML file, no network access; download it and open it in a browser): https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/blob/1acd3beb0b0e9378b06074e3e2615ba7cd5d89f4/tool-library-proposal/mockup.html

## What we have today

- "Tool library" is a tab beside Properties (`tool_library::draw`). It lists the built-in catalog with an "Add" button.
- A tool is edited on a property page with four folded groups: Geometry, Holder, Cutting data and Catalog (`tool_settings_grid::grid`).
- The holder is a combo box inside the tool (`tool_holder_picker`). The holder library is built in (`holder_library.rs`).
- The tool drawing is a 260 px square (`tool_preview::draw`).
- The cutting data of a tool is a table of `CuttingRow` entries, one for each work material.

## The proposal

### 1. One dialog, opened from the ribbon

- The **Tools** cell of the ribbon opens the dialog. The tab on the right side goes away.
- The header has a switch: **Tools | Holders**.
- The first screen is a list. Categories are on the left. Items are on the right.
- A click on an item opens its editor. The list folds into a narrow rail on the left. The user can go from item to item in the rail. An arrow goes back to the full list.

### 2. Tools

- The list has three sources: Document, My library and Catalog.
- Each row shows: a small drawing, the T number, the name, the type, the diameter, the flute length, the number of flutes, the holder, the gauge length and the number of recipes.
- The editor has three tabs: **Tool**, **Recipes** and **Details**.
- The parameters are on the left. The drawing is on the right.

### 3. Holders are first-class items

- Holders have their own list. The list is grouped by spindle taper.
- Each row shows: the name, the taper, the clamp, the clamping range, the gauge length, the largest diameter and the number of tools that use the holder.
- A holder has its own editor: the machine side (taper), the tool side (clamp and clamping range) and the shape.
- The holder editor lists the tools that use the holder. A change to the holder updates each of these tools in one undo step.
- The list shows which taper the mounted machine takes. The holder picker of a tool marks the holders with a different taper.

### 4. One home for each field

Today some values are in two places. The proposal gives each value one owner:

| Owner | Fields |
|---|---|
| Tool | Cutter (diameter, flute length, corner radius, angles, flutes, helix, tool material) and shank diameter |
| Holder | Taper, clamp, clamping range, gauge length of the holder, largest diameter, shape |
| Assembly (tool in holder) | The holder that the tool uses, and the stick-out |

- The assembly is one boxed group at the bottom of the Tool tab.
- The gauge length of the assembly is not typed. The dialog shows it: holder gauge length + stick-out.
- The same group shows if the shank diameter is in the clamping range of the holder.
- A link in the group opens the holder in its editor.

### 5. A large drawing

- The drawing is to scale, from the tool tip to the spindle nose.
- It shows the cutter, the shank and the holder.
- It shows dimension lines: diameter, flute length, stick-out, gauge length and shank diameter.
- It shows the flutes as helix lines, from `flutes` and `helix_deg`. This is decoration only. It adds no geometry law.
- The user can switch off the dimensions, the holder and the flutes.
- The drawing changes when the user changes a value.

### 6. Recipes

- The **Recipes** tab shows one row for each work material: spindle speed, feed, stepdown and stepover.
- Below each row the dialog shows the surface speed and the feed per tooth.
- A mark shows the row of the work material of the document. Operations use that row.
- Buttons: "Add material", "Suggest feeds and speeds" and "Copy recipes from tool".
- The data is the `CuttingRow` table of today. Plasma and waterjet tools keep their own recipe columns.

## What does not change

- Each Apply is one undoable command: `AddTool`, `ChangeTool`, `SetToolBody`, `ApplyCuttingData`. The MCP tools stay as they are.
- The file formats (`.camtools`, PathPilot `.csv`, Hurco `.TCM`) stay as they are.
- The page tests `layout_page_tool` and `layout_page_tool_library` need a new home as `layout_window_*` tests.

## Relation to open issues

- #3645 (user library store): "My library" needs it. This dialog is its front end.
- #3648 (component library browser) and #808 (holder library follow-ups): the Holders list and editor.
- #2452 and #3642 to #3647 (component-based tool assemblies, ISO 13399): a tool, a holder and a stick-out are the smallest assembly. The assembly group can grow into the assembly editor (extensions, inserts).
- #3393 (cut recipes GUI): the Recipes tab.
- #93 (spun design editor): "Edit outline" in the holder editor can open it.

## Open questions

1. Dialog or dockable window: can the user keep it open beside the viewport?
2. User-made holders need a store and a file format. Is that part of #3645?
3. Is a recipe one row for each material on the tool, as today? Or is it a shared object with a name (#3393)?
4. Does this dialog become the assembly editor of #2452?
5. Which part is the first slice? Suggestion: the dialog with the Tools list and the editor, on the data model of today. Holders and "My library" follow when their stores exist.

## Notes

- The mock-up uses the default dark theme tokens and the tool fields of `main`.
- No material of another CAM product was used.
- The pictures are mock-ups made in HTML. They are not pictures of the application.

    error[E0462]: found staticlib `zerocopy` instead of rlib or dylib which `camcraft_app` depends on
    error[E0786]: found invalid metadata files for crate `accesskit` which `camcraft_ui` depends on
    error[E0786]: found invalid metadata files for crate `test`

Each run then shows many errors of the form `error[E0463]: can't find crate for 'camcraft_ui'` (or `camcraft_app`). Those follow from the first error. The 8 integration suites after the failed build still ran and passed in each run.

## Conditions
- Windows 11 Home 10.0.26300, 16 logical CPUs, local disk.
- rustc 1.99.1 (58cf8f9c3 2026-10-13), cargo 1.99.1, target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.
- The gate sets `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0` for each cargo step. I set no other build variable.

- Two different branches, both based on `main` 4c0a157e1, gave the same result.
- `cargo clean -p camcraft-ui` before a run did not help.
- I started no other cargo command at the same time as these runs.

## Runs
| Run | Job budget | Build step |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 16 | fail (`png`) |
| 2 | 16 | fail (`zerocopy`) |
| 3 | 16, after `cargo clean -p camcraft-ui` | fail (`accesskit`) |

| 7 | 4 (`CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=4`), later run on the first branch | ok |
| 8 | 4 (`CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=4`), later run on the second branch | ok |

title: Rotary ops refuse a helical part (screw rotor) on an A table: the axis is fitted from the normals only, never taken from the machine's rotary line

labels.name: enhancement

labels.name: source:agent

body:
Reported by flamingfire (Discord, relayed by the user, 2026-11-19), v0.24.0 (f2d78f31), Windows.

## What happens

Project `Rotor.camproj`: model `WVF350-101-453`, a long helical rotor (screw-compressor style lobes, shaft ends) laid along X; machine Doosan DNM 5700 + rotary table (A about X), Fanuc post; one 6 mm ball nose; a box stock around the part. Rotary Parallel1 (Source: Stock) and Rotary Contour1 both refuse:

```
generate failed: could not generate the toolpath: Rotary Parallel1: invalid machining parameters: the model's normals share no rotation axis - a turned workpiece is rotary work; finish a freeform with the 5-Axis kinds
```

The refusal is correct for today's design (the rotary operations fit the axis of revolution from the mesh normals, and a helicoid has no common axis). But this part is classic **4-axis wrap work**: it is clamped in the A axis on its own centreline, A turns and the tool follows the lobes. The user has a 4-axis machine, not a 5-axis one, so the message's advice ("finish a freeform with the 5-Axis kinds") does not help.

## Wanted

1. When the model is not a solid of revolution, the rotary operations can take the axis from the setup instead: the mounted machine's rotary line (A about X) through the WCS / a stated centre (e.g. the stock's or the shaft ends' fitted axis), stated by the user, not guessed.
2. Rotary Parallel (and Rotary Offset roughing) then wrap the toolpath round that axis with the existing radial field check (gouge against the fitted skin = the model itself, stock, part), so a helical rotor, auger, fluted shaft or cam with non-turned features can be finished on 4 axes.
3. Until then, the refusal message names the 4-axis case: e.g. "the model is not a shape of revolution; rotary operations need one today (#this). A part clamped on A that is not turned (helical lobes) is not supported yet" - not only the 5-axis pointer.

## Notes

- The shaft ends of this model are turned; only the lobes are helical. The ends alone would fit an axis, so "fit the axis from the turned faces only" could be a first step.
- Safety floor: the axis must be stated or fitted from real turned faces; a guessed axis that is off by a fraction of a mm wraps a gouge. Refuse when the stated axis and the turned faces disagree.
- Clean-room: published 4-axis wrapping literature only.

Done means: the reporter's kind of part (helical lobes between turned ends, on A about X) generates a Rotary Parallel finish that passes the radial gouge check and posts on the Doosan/Fanuc posts; a part with no turned faces and no stated axis is still refused, with a message that names the 4-axis case.

body:
## What happens

Small drill-cycle readings from the QA run, checked on upstream main abe24ff09 (`crates/motion/src/drilling/hole.rs` `auto_kind`, `cycle.rs`):

1. **Auto counts the air above the hole as depth.** The auto law reads depth as R plane - bottom. With Top Z at top_of_model (z 15) and holes starting at z 10 and 7, a 3.5 mm spot (bottom z 6.5 / 3.5) reads as 8.5 / 11.5 mm deep and resolves to a chip-break peck: `G73 X8 Y8 Z-10.5 R-2 Q18 F300` (Q = 3 x d = 18, more than the whole depth). A 3.5 mm spot should be G81 (or G82 with a dwell).
2. **No way to ask for G83.** The `cycle` choices are auto, spot, drill, peck, tap, bore, back_bore, floating_tap, ream. `peck` is always the chip-break G73; the full-retract G83 (`CycleKind::Deep`) is reachable only through auto when depth > 4 x d. A user who wants full retracts in a deep or gummy hole cannot say so.
3. **The choices are not listed.** `list_operation_types` shows `cycle` as a string with default `auto`, without the allowed words, so an agent does not find `spot` (which exists and would have served the QA run's spot drilling, see #897).

## Expected

Auto measures depth from the hole's entry (or the material top over it), not from the R plane; an explicit full-retract choice (e.g. `deep`) posts G83; `list_operation_types` lists the cycle words.

Repro: **Part (p01-flange):** 6061 plate 100 x 60 x 10 mm centred on the origin (z 0..10), a 60 x 30 x 5 mm island on top (z 10..15, R5 corners) with a 1 x 45 deg chamfer on its top edges, 4 x dia 6 through holes at (+-42, +-22), a 10 mm wide x 3 mm deep slot across the +X end (x 35..45, floor z 7). Stock: box fitted to the model with +2 mm on top (100 x 60 x 17, z 0..17). WCS G54 at the stock's min-X min-Y top corner, world (-50, -30, 17). Machine Tormach 770MX, post Tormach PathPilot. Then a Drill with any tool on the detected holes, `cycle: "auto"`, a hole floor 3.5 mm below its entry; `post {post: "Tormach PathPilot"}`.

P7: the posted cycles are legal and cut the right depth; this is wording and choice.

Found by the QA swarm (SolidCraft v0.44.1 + CamCraft v0.23.0, part p01-flange). Re-checked on upstream main abe24ff09.

**Done means:** a 3.5 mm spot under a 5 mm air gap posts G81/G82 under auto; `cycle: "deep"` (or the chosen word) posts G83; `list_operation_types` lists the cycle words; tests pin each.

title: Process changes - fork maintainers please subscribe

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: P?
labels.description: Paused: never picked until the maintainer sets a real priority

body:
**Subscribe to this issue** (the "Subscribe" button on the right) if you work from a fork of CamCraft, especially with an AI agent.

Forks sync product code only at release tags (AGENTS.md "A fork syncs from upstream at each cut tag"). But the *process* - `AGENTS.md`, the agent definitions in `.claude/agents/`, the skills in `.claude/skills/` and `scripts/gate.*` - changes between releases, and a fork's agents should follow the current rules (review labels, priority labels, release steps, and so on).

**How it works:**
- `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` holds one number. Every PR that changes a process file bumps it.
- Every such PR also adds a comment **here**: the new version, what changed, and what to pull. Subscribers get one notification per change.
- A fork's agent compares its `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` with upstream's at the start of each session and, if upstream is newer, pulls just the process files (AGENTS.md "Process files sync on every session"). Product code still waits for the next release tag.

**To pull by hand:**
```
git fetch upstream
git checkout upstream/main -- AGENTS.md .claude/agents .claude/skills .claude/PROCESS_VERSION scripts/gate.ps1 scripts/gate.sh
git commit -m "chore(process): sync process files to upstream PROCESS_VERSION <n>"
```

This issue stays open and pinned. It's labelled `P?` so no agent ever picks it up as work.
